newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Profits of S.Korea petrochem firms seen picking up.
newsitem.headline: Profits of S.Korea petrochem firms seen picking up.

text.p: South Korean petrochemical companies, buoyed by tight petrochemical supply and weak naphtha prices, are likely to see profits recover this year, industry analysts said on Monday.
Shares of petrochemical stocks are benefiting from the rosy prospects, leading the composite index to a higher close on Monday.
"Strong petrochemical product prices in the first half will benefit petrochemical firms' overall profits for this year," said Han Yong, an energy analyst at Jardine Fleming Securities.
Profits of major petrochemical companies were lower last year due to poor petrochemical product prices and high naphtha prices, analysts said.

Jardine Fleming's Han said he expects LG Chemical Ltd to post a net profit of between 20 billion and 25 billion won this year, up from 3.3 billion won last year. Hanwha Chemical Corp is seen reporting a 10 billion won in net profits against a 25.6 billion won net loss in 1996, he said.

Analysts said a concentration of plant maintenance shutdowns in the second quarter of 1997 is tightening petrochemical supply and slowing demand for naphtha, a feed stock for most petrochemical products.
Falling crude oil prices are mainly behind the slide in naphtha prices.

The regional price of naphtha is currently at $210 a tonne Cost and Freight (C&F), down 10 percent from the end of last year, industry sources said. Meawhile, prices of ethylene have risen 30 percent to $630 a tonne C&F.
Analysts said petrochemical prices were expected to peak in the second quarter and then consolidate, while naphtha prices would stay soft for the rest of this year.
"Prices of petrochemical products are expected to consolidate in the future but not so as to erode margins," said Lee Sang-koo, a petrochemical analyst at Hyundai Securities.
"Profit margins will improve on the strength of a much greater fall in naphtha prices than in petrochemical product prices," he said.
Analysts said growing demand from abroad, especially China, would help boost exports.
"Since China's economy is expected to grow at more than 10 percent during the first half, demand for petrochemical products should increase further," said Lee of Hyundai Securities.
Petrochemical share prices are also expected to gain on positive earnings growth, analysts said.
"Petrochemical shares were a main contributor to Monday's rise," said Lee Young-won, a broker at Daewoo Securities.
The composite stock index closed at 704.20 points on Monday, up 7.25.
Honam Petrochemical Corp, the biggest gainer among petrochemical stocks, rose to its daily limit high of 14,600 won, up 1,000.
